text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher with July rising to nearly eight-week highs on the back of fund and roaster buying. The rise came as a belated reaction to New York's arabica futures advance on Monday.

The ICO export figures for March underline the heavy front-loading of exports by ICO member countries following a price rally earlier this year. Exports totalled 7.41 mn 60-kg bags in March, up sharply from 6.47 mn in March 1996. May and July closed $35 higher at $1,635 and $1,705 per tonne respectively. Arabica futures in New York settled sharply lower on speculative long-liquidation in a technical correction to the market's recent rise.

News that Colombia's truck drivers threatened to launch another nation-wide strike could not halt the decline. Benchmark July closed 5.65 cents/lb lower at 212.85 cents/lb, while September gave up 4.70 cents/lb to close at 190.15 cents/lb. However, tight arabica supplies are likely to continue to support prices and additionally, traders said they will continue to keep an eye on strike developments in Colombia.

However, Colombian truck drivers lifted their day-old strike in the Caribbean port of Cartagena on May 6, partially dispelling fears that the action could spread to the rest of the country. However, any disruption to the flow of supply at a time when inventories are already at low levels will have to be viewed as supportive. After Tuesday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks dropped by 13,999 bags to 27,699 bags as of May 5. There were 11,250 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said. Sentiment remains bullish and most analysts expect prices to rise in the weeks/months ahead.

ICO - Coffee exports by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization rose to 7.406 mn bags in March 1997 from 6.470 mn bags the same month the previous year, the International Coffee Organization said. That brought total exports in October/March 1996/97 up to 42.634 mn bags, up nearly 16 per cent from the 36.783 mn bags shipped the same period in 1995/96. Brazil's market share in October/March 1996/97 rose dramatically to 23.89 per cent from 15.16 per cent in 1995/96. By contrast Colombia's market share fell to 13.97 per cent from 15.92 per cent in 1995/96. Based on ICO export data, shipments so far are well ahead of a year-ago levels and are at a record level surpassing the period of heavy de-stocking in 1989/90. This should limit supplies for the remainder of the year. Much of the increase was absorbed based on the limited increase seen in European and US stock data in recent months relative to the heavy volumes exported. POLAND - Poland imported 147,952 bags of coffee in October 1996, nearly 8 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.367 mn bags, nearly 6 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose to 1.536 mn bags, up from 1.442 mn bags imported the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Ivory Coast (177,800 vs 174,000 bags), Peru (109,300 vs 122,300 bags), India (160,800 vs 97,700 bags), Indonesia (304,900 vs 158,200 bags) and Vietnam (153,900 vs 229,400 bags). The country exported 74,100 bags of coffee in January/October 1995, significantly up on the 37,600 bags exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 rose to 42,300 bags from 17,000 bags in 1994.

AUSTRALIA - Australia imported 161,100 bags of coffee in January/February 1997, 8 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 3.7 per cent to 845,200 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/February 1997 were Vietnam (55,100 vs 53,200 bags) and Papua New Guinea (41,500 vs 37,100 bags).
